subject: general
question: Which of the following is the first World Bank supported programme for minority welfare that is being implemented by the Ministry of Minority Welfare, Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nai Manzil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nai Manzil** is the first World Bank supported programme for minority welfare being implemented by the Ministry of Minority Welfare, Government of India.
 
• The programme aims to provide education and skill training to the minority youth, thereby improving their employability and livelihood opportunities.
 
• It focuses on bridging the academic and skill development gaps among minority communities.
 
• The initiative includes components such as providing non-residential training, placement support, and tracking of trainees for a year post-training.
 
• Nai Manzil targets school dropouts and those in the age group of 17-35 years from minority communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Minority Welfare, Government of India, was established to ensure a more focused approach towards issues relating to the minorities.
 
• Other schemes under the Ministry include **Naya Savera**, which provides free coaching for minority students, and **Nai Udaan**, which offers financial support for minority students clearing prelims of Group A and B examinations conducted by UPSC, SSC, and State Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Padho Pardesh** is another scheme that provides interest subsidies on educational loans for overseas studies for students belonging to minority communities.
 
• The World Bank's involvement in Nai Manzil highlights the international support and collaboration in improving the socio-economic conditions of minority communities in India.
